title: Repository skeleton and Debian packaging stub
prompt:
Create the vintner-boot repository skeleton described in docs/architecture.md §11, plus a minimal Debian source-package skeleton.

Context: docs/architecture.md (revision 1.1) is the source of truth. Read §5 (package boundaries), §11 (repository outline) and §16 (open decisions) before starting. No implementation language has been chosen yet (ADR-0002 is open), so this task creates structure and documentation only.

Do:
- Create every directory in the §11 tree that does not exist yet: schema/, src/, firmware/{uefi,bios,experimental-limine}/, integration/{kernel-hooks,initramfs-hooks,systemd-units,installer}/, recovery/{kernel-config,initramfs,tools,tests}/, graphics/plymouth-theme/, examples/{disk-layouts,configs}/.
- Put one README.md in each of those directories: 2-5 sentences stating what belongs there, citing the relevant architecture.md section (e.g. "§4.1"). Write plain, complete sentences. Do not invent design details that are not in architecture.md.
- src/README.md must state that the language and layout are set by ADR-0002 (open) and that no code goes here until it is accepted.
- Create debian/ as a Debian source package (debhelper compat 13, source format "3.0 (native)", Section admin, Priority optional, Maintainer "zcomputerwiz <zcomputerwiz@users.noreply.github.com>") with exactly three binary packages: vintner-core, vintner-platform, vintner-installer. All Architecture: all, empty for now, with short and long descriptions taken from architecture.md §5. debian/changelog: one entry, version 0.0.0, distribution UNRELEASED. debian/copyright in DEP-5 format, GPL-2 for the whole tree (the repo LICENSE is GPL-2.0).

Do not:
- add Depends, Conflicts, maintainer scripts, systemd units or any code; package relations land with WP-005
- touch docs/, README.md, LICENSE, .gitignore, ci/, third_party/, .github/ or .jules/
- add dependencies or build tooling beyond debhelper

Acceptance: on a Debian 13 or Ubuntu 24.04 system with `debhelper` and `dpkg-dev` installed, `dpkg-buildpackage -us -uc -b` run from the repository root exits 0 and produces vintner-core_0.0.0_all.deb, vintner-platform_0.0.0_all.deb and vintner-installer_0.0.0_all.deb in the parent directory. Paste the command output into the PR description.

title: Phase-0 QEMU OVMF/SeaBIOS baseline harness
prompt:
Build the phase-0 QEMU boot baseline harness (WP-001, first slice) for vintner-boot: boot an unmodified Debian 13 cloud image under OVMF (Secure Boot off and on) and SeaBIOS, and record serial logs.

Context: docs/architecture.md §9 (phase 0) and §10 (test plan) describe the goal. This slice only proves that stock Debian 13 boots under each firmware and captures evidence; it does not install anything from this repository.

Do:
- ci/lib/fetch-image.sh: download the Debian 13 "genericcloud" amd64 qcow2 from https://cloud.debian.org/images/cloud/trixie/ using a pinned dated release directory (not "latest"), verify it against the SHA512SUMS file from the same directory, cache it under ci/out/cache/ and never modify the cached file (boot from a qcow2 overlay instead).
- ci/qemu-ovmf/boot-baseline.sh with `--secure-boot on|off`: boot the image with q35, OVMF 4M code/vars from the distribution `ovmf` package (copy the vars file per run; for Secure Boot use the secboot code file and the Microsoft-keys vars file), serial on stdio captured to ci/out/<run-name>/serial.log.
- ci/qemu-seabios/boot-baseline.sh: same, with SeaBIOS (QEMU default BIOS).
- Each script: use KVM when /dev/kvm is usable, otherwise TCG with a longer timeout; pass when the serial log shows the login prompt (or cloud-init's "Cloud-init ... finished" line) within the timeout; then power the VM off and exit 0; on timeout kill QEMU and exit 1. Record QEMU version, firmware file paths with sha256, image sha512, accelerator and boot time in ci/out/<run-name>/summary.txt.
- .github/workflows/qemu-baseline.yml: on push and pull_request, ubuntu-24.04, install qemu-system-x86 ovmf, enable KVM via the documented udev rule for GitHub-hosted runners, run the three cases as a matrix, upload ci/out/ (excluding the image cache) as artifacts. Cache the downloaded image with actions/cache keyed on the pinned image path.
- ci/README.md: how to run each case locally, required packages, and what is recorded.
- Add ci/out/ to .gitignore.

Do not:
- touch docs/, debian/, src/, schema/, firmware/, integration/, recovery/, third_party/ or .jules/
- modify the Debian image contents, inject keys, or build anything from this repo
- use Docker or add language runtimes; POSIX sh or bash plus coreutils, curl, qemu only

Acceptance: `shellcheck ci/**/*.sh` is clean, and `ci/qemu-seabios/boot-baseline.sh`, `ci/qemu-ovmf/boot-baseline.sh --secure-boot off` and `ci/qemu-ovmf/boot-baseline.sh --secure-boot on` each exit 0 locally. Paste each summary.txt into the PR description.

title: third_party pin manifest and verify script
prompt:
Create the vintner-boot third_party/ pin manifest and license inventory, with a script that verifies every pin against its upstream.

Context: docs/architecture.md §7 (adoption decisions), §12 and §14 (source index) list the upstream projects. Phase 0 (§9) requires pinned references and license notes. third_party/ holds pins and metadata only, never copies of upstream source.

Do:
- third_party/pins.tsv, tab-separated with a header row: name, kind (git|debian), location (git URL, or Debian source package name), ref (git tag/branch, or Debian version), commit (full 40-character SHA for git; "-" for debian), spdx (license expression), role (adopt|evaluate|reference, from §7).
- Git pins (resolve each tag to its commit with `git ls-remote`, do not guess SHAs): systemd at the upstream tag matching Debian 13's systemd 257.13; GRUB tag grub-2.12; shim tag 16.1; Limine latest tag on the v12.x branch; RAUC latest release tag; dracut-ng latest release tag; Plymouth latest release tag; u-root latest release tag; U-Boot tag v2026.04; Heads master; Petitboot master; ReactOS master. For branch pins (master), record today's commit and say "branch snapshot" in role.
- Debian pins for trixie (Debian 13) current versions: systemd (source of systemd-boot-efi, systemd-boot-efi-amd64-signed, systemd-ukify), shim-signed, grub2, initramfs-tools, plymouth, ovmf (edk2), linux. Look versions up from https://sources.debian.org/api/src/<package>/ or packages.debian.org; do not guess.
- third_party/verify.sh (POSIX sh): for every git row, check with `git ls-remote` that ref still resolves to the recorded commit; for every debian row, check via https://sources.debian.org/api/src/<package>/ that the recorded version exists. Print one line per row (OK/MISMATCH/MISSING) and exit non-zero on any failure.
- third_party/README.md: what each column means, how to bump a pin (edit row, run verify.sh), and a license summary table (project, SPDX, how vintner-boot uses it: payload / build tool / reference only), consistent with the licensing note in architecture.md §7.

Do not:
- vendor, clone into the repo, or copy any upstream source
- touch any path outside third_party/
- invent commit SHAs or versions; every value must come from a command or page you actually queried

Acceptance: `sh third_party/verify.sh` exits 0 and prints OK for every row; `shellcheck third_party/verify.sh` is clean. Paste the verify.sh output into the PR description.

title: Survey Debian 13 packages that write bootloaders
prompt:
Find every Debian 13 (trixie) package whose maintainer scripts or kernel/initramfs hooks can write a bootloader, boot entries or NVRAM, and commit a reproducible script plus its report.

Context: docs/architecture.md §5 (last paragraph of "Package manager interactions") requires a lifecycle test that installs, upgrades and removes every package whose maintainer scripts call `grub-install`, `update-grub`, `bootctl install`/`update` or `efibootmgr`. This task produces that package list. It is research plus one script; nothing is installed on a target system.

Do:
- ci/lifecycle/find-boot-writers.sh (bash, plus curl, xz/gzip, awk, dpkg-deb; no other runtimes):
  1. Download `dists/trixie/Release`, `dists/trixie/<component>/Contents-amd64.gz` and `dists/trixie/<component>/binary-amd64/Packages.xz` from https://deb.debian.org/debian for components main, contrib, non-free, non-free-firmware. Verify each index's SHA256 against the Release file. Cache downloads under ci/out/cache/lifecycle/.
  2. Build the candidate set as the union of:
     (a) packages shipping any file under etc/kernel/ (postinst.d, postrm.d, preinst.d, prerm.d, install.d, install.conf), etc/initramfs/post-update.d/, usr/lib/kernel/install.d/, usr/share/initramfs-tools/hooks/ that mentions a matched command, or etc/grub.d/;
     (b) packages that Depends, Pre-Depends or Recommends any of: grub-common, grub2-common, grub-pc, grub-pc-bin, grub-efi-amd64, grub-efi-amd64-bin, grub-efi-amd64-signed, shim-signed, efibootmgr, systemd-boot, systemd-boot-efi, systemd-ukify, dracut, initramfs-tools;
     (c) the packages named in (b) themselves.
  3. Download each candidate .deb (current trixie version from Packages.xz), extract its control members (preinst, postinst, prerm, postrm, config, triggers) and the hook files from (a), and search them for: grub-install, update-grub, grub-mkconfig, grub-set-default, grub-reboot, grub-editenv, bootctl, efibootmgr, kernel-install, update-initramfs, dracut, ukify. Also record `interest`/`activate` trigger names from the triggers file.
  4. Write ci/lifecycle/boot-writers-trixie.tsv with a header row: package, version, member (e.g. postinst or the hook path), command, line (line number), excerpt (the matched line, tabs replaced by spaces). One row per match. Sort by package, member, line.
- ci/lifecycle/README.md: what the script does, how to rerun it, the Release file Date and the index SHA256 values used for the committed report, and a short summary table: package, which commands it calls, and from where (maintainer script or hook). Mark each package as "writes loader/NVRAM" (grub-install, bootctl install/update, efibootmgr writes), "writes boot config" (update-grub, grub-mkconfig, grub-set-default, grub-reboot, grub-editenv, kernel-install) or "regenerates initramfs only".

Do not:
- touch any path outside ci/lifecycle/ (in particular not ci/README.md, ci/lib/, ci/qemu-*, .github/, .gitignore, docs/, debian/, third_party/ or .jules/)
- commit downloaded .deb files or indexes; only the script, the TSV report and the README
- hand-edit the TSV; it must be exactly what the script produces

Acceptance: `shellcheck ci/lifecycle/find-boot-writers.sh` is clean; `bash ci/lifecycle/find-boot-writers.sh` exits 0 and regenerates the committed TSV byte-for-byte; the report includes at least these known positives, and if any is missing the script is wrong: grub-pc (postinst calls grub-install), grub-efi-amd64 (postinst calls grub-install), shim-signed (postinst calls grub-install), grub-common or grub2-common (kernel hook calling update-grub), systemd-boot (kernel and initramfs hooks). Paste the README summary table and the script's final line counts into the PR description.

title: OVMF Secure Boot variable stores
prompt:
Generate the OVMF Secure Boot variable stores that the vintner-boot CI matrix needs, using virt-fw-vars, with a script that rebuilds them from pinned certificates.

Context: docs/architecture.md §10 (Firmware axis) requires OVMF variable stores whose `db` holds: only the Microsoft UEFI CA 2011, only the 2023 CA, both, and a project test key. §8 explains why (the 2011 CA expired June 27, 2026). Stores are built with `virt-fw-vars` from `python3-virt-firmware`. This task only builds and inspects the stores; booting them belongs to the QEMU harness, which is being written separately under ci/qemu-ovmf/.

Do:
- ci/ovmf-vars/certs/: the Microsoft certificates as PEM, taken from https://github.com/microsoft/secureboot_objects pinned to one commit (record the commit). Needed: Microsoft Corporation KEK CA 2011, Microsoft Corporation KEK 2K CA 2023, Microsoft Windows Production PCA 2011, Windows UEFI CA 2023, Microsoft Corporation UEFI CA 2011, Microsoft UEFI CA 2023. ci/ovmf-vars/certs/SHA256SUMS lists each file; the script verifies it before use.
- ci/ovmf-vars/make-vars.sh (bash): starting from the distribution's empty 4M vars template (`OVMF_VARS_4M.fd` from the `ovmf` package; find the path on Ubuntu 24.04 and Debian 13), produce in ci/out/ovmf-vars/:
  - `vars-ms2011.fd`: KEK = KEK CA 2011; db = Windows Production PCA 2011 + UEFI CA 2011
  - `vars-ms2023.fd`: KEK = KEK 2K CA 2023; db = Windows UEFI CA 2023 + UEFI CA 2023
  - `vars-ms-both.fd`: union of the two above
  - `vars-project-test.fd`: as `vars-ms-both.fd`, plus a project test certificate in db
  - `vars-setup-mode.fd`: no PK, no keys (setup mode), for enrollment tests
  Each store except setup mode gets a freshly generated test PK and Secure Boot enabled. Generate the test PK and the project test key with openssl (RSA 2048, SHA-256, 10-year validity, CN "vintner-boot CI test PK" / "vintner-boot CI test db key") into ci/out/ovmf-vars/keys/ on every run. Write the public certificates next to the stores so later CI steps can sign test images.
- After building, the script runs `virt-fw-dump` (or the equivalent in the installed virt-firmware version) on each store and checks the expected certificate subjects are present in PK, KEK and db and that no unexpected ones are, exiting non-zero on any mismatch. Write the dump of each store to ci/out/ovmf-vars/<store>.txt.
- ci/ovmf-vars/README.md: required packages, how to run, what each store contains and which §10 row it serves, where the private test keys go, and the secureboot_objects commit.

Do not:
- commit any private key, generated key or generated .fd file; only the script, the README and the PEM certificates with SHA256SUMS
- set DBX or SBAT levels (separate task), or modify the OVMF code files
- touch any path outside ci/ovmf-vars/ (in particular not ci/README.md, ci/lib/, ci/qemu-*, .github/, .gitignore, docs/, debian/, third_party/ or .jules/)
- use Docker or add language runtimes beyond what python3-virt-firmware itself needs

Acceptance: on Ubuntu 24.04 with `ovmf python3-virt-firmware openssl` installed, `shellcheck ci/ovmf-vars/make-vars.sh` is clean and `bash ci/ovmf-vars/make-vars.sh` exits 0, producing all five stores with passing subject checks. Paste the PK/KEK/db subject list of each store from the dumps into the PR description.

title: Measure Debian 13 boot image sizes
prompt:
Measure real Debian 13 boot image sizes so the vintner-boot image budget in docs/architecture.md §5 can replace its placeholders.

Context: §5 "Image budget" sizes the boot storage partition from placeholder values (150 MiB per ordinary UKI or BIOS slot, 300 MiB per recovery image). WP-002 (§13) requires measured sizes. Ordinary images are a Debian kernel plus its initramfs-tools initramfs, packed as a UKI with ukify on UEFI (§4) or kept as a kernel+initramfs pair on BIOS.

Do:
- ci/measure/image-sizes.sh (bash; mmdebstrap or debootstrap, plus coreutils; run with sudo where needed): create a Debian 13 (trixie) amd64 chroot under ci/out/measure/, install `linux-image-amd64 initramfs-tools systemd-ukify systemd-boot-efi zstd`, and measure, in bytes:
  1. /boot/vmlinuz-<ABI>
  2. the initramfs with Debian defaults (MODULES=most, COMPRESS as shipped)
  3. the initramfs with MODULES=dep is not meaningful in a chroot, so instead MODULES=list with an empty modules list (lower bound)
  4. a UKI built with `ukify build --linux ... --initrd ... --cmdline "root=PARTUUID=00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000 ro quiet" --os-release @/etc/os-release` using the trixie systemd-stub, for both initramfs variants
  5. `/lib/modules/<ABI>` total size (for the module-tree discussion in §6.1)
  6. systemd-bootx64.efi from systemd-boot-efi, and if available in trixie the signed variants from systemd-boot-efi-amd64-signed and shim-signed (download the .deb and extract; do not install shim-signed)
  Record the exact package versions (`dpkg-query -W`) for everything measured.
- Write ci/out/measure/sizes.tsv (name, bytes, MiB to 1 decimal, package version) and print it.
- ci/measure/README.md: how to run, what each row means, and a results table copied from one run on the date you ran it, plus the arithmetic from §5 redone with the measured ordinary-image size (3 ordinary images + 1 staging + 2 recovery at the 300 MiB placeholder, + 20% margin).

Do not:
- touch any path outside ci/measure/ (in particular not docs/, ci/README.md, ci/lib/, ci/qemu-*, .github/, .gitignore, debian/, third_party/ or .jules/)
- commit the chroot or any generated image
- change docs/architecture.md; the maintainers will update §5 from your numbers

Acceptance: `shellcheck ci/measure/image-sizes.sh` is clean and `sudo bash ci/measure/image-sizes.sh` exits 0 on Ubuntu 24.04 and prints the table. Paste the table and the package versions into the PR description.

title: systemd-boot selection policy QEMU test
prompt:
Build a QEMU/OVMF test that proves how Debian 13's systemd-boot selects vintner UKI entries: sort order, boot counting, the all-bad case, foreign entries and EFI variable overrides.

Context: read docs/adr/0003-uefi-entry-naming-and-boot-counting.md first. It lists eight findings from the systemd v257 source and fixes the entry names and .osrel fields. firmware/uefi/loader.conf is the loader.conf under test. docs/architecture.md §4.1, §10 ("Selection policy") and §12 risk 10 explain why this must be proven on the real binary. This test is standalone: it does not boot Debian and does not use the ci/qemu-ovmf/ harness that is being written separately.

Do:
- ci/selection-policy/build.sh (bash): fetch from Debian trixie (deb.debian.org, current trixie versions; record them) the packages systemd-boot-efi, systemd-ukify, linux-image-amd64 (resolve to the real linux-image-<ABI> package) and busybox-static. Extract them with `dpkg-deb -x` into ci/out/selection-policy/debs/ (or use an mmdebstrap trixie chroot if that is simpler). Use the trixie systemd-bootx64.efi and linuxx64.efi.stub, never the host's.
- A tiny test initramfs (cpio, busybox-static): /init mounts proc, sys and efivarfs, prints exactly one line `VINTNER-TEST-BOOTED id=<vintner.test_id from /proc/cmdline>` to /dev/ttyS0, then does what `vintner.test_action=` says: `poweroff` (default) or `reboot` (simulates a failed boot). It may also print the LoaderEntrySelected EFI variable in the same line.
- Build test UKIs with the trixie ukify and stub, command line `console=ttyS0 vintner.test_id=<id> vintner.test_action=<action>`, and an `--os-release` file whose IMAGE_ID, IMAGE_VERSION and PRETTY_NAME follow the ADR-0003 table (ordinary: IMAGE_ID=vintner-os, IMAGE_VERSION=<gen>; recovery: IMAGE_ID=vintner-recovery-a / vintner-recovery-b). Foreign test UKIs use IMAGE_ID unset and ID=debian.
- A disk image built without root (sfdisk plus mtools with `-i image@@offset`): GPT with an ESP (FAT32, 64 MiB) holding \EFI\BOOT\BOOTX64.EFI and \EFI\vintner\systemd-bootx64.efi (both the trixie systemd-bootx64.efi) and \loader\loader.conf copied from firmware/uefi/loader.conf; and an XBOOTLDR partition (GPT type bc13c2ff-59e6-4262-a352-b275fd6f7172, FAT32, 256 MiB) holding /EFI/Linux/*.efi.
- ci/selection-policy/run.sh (bash): for each scenario, build a fresh disk and a fresh copy of the OVMF 4M vars (non-Secure-Boot code file from the host `ovmf` package), boot with qemu-system-x86_64 -machine q35 -nographic -serial file:..., KVM if /dev/kvm is usable, else TCG; follow reboots up to the scenario's boot count with a per-boot timeout; after each boot list /EFI/Linux on both partitions with `mdir` and record which test id booted. Scenarios (file names per ADR-0003; "+3" means a fresh counter):
  S1 order: os-2+3, os-1 (no counter), recovery-a+3, recovery-b → boots os-2; afterwards os-2 is renamed +2-1.
  S2 failing candidate: os-2+1-2 (action reboot), os-1 → boot 1 is os-2 and it becomes +0-3; boot 2 is os-1.
  S3 all ordinary bad: os-2+0-3, os-1+0-3, recovery-a+3, recovery-b → recovery-a, with no input.
  S4 recovery A bad too: as S3 with recovery-a+0-3 → recovery-b.
  S5 foreign entries: S1 plus a foreign UKI debian-6.12.efi in /EFI/Linux on the ESP and on XBOOTLDR, and a Type #1 entry /loader/entries/aaa.conf on the ESP pointing at the foreign UKI → still os-2.
  S6 counter grows from many boots: os-1+3 with action reboot only → os-1 boots three times (+2-1, +1-2, +0-3), then recovery-a.
  S7 LoaderEntryDefault: S1 with LoaderEntryDefault (vendor GUID 4a67b082-0a4c-41cf-b6c7-440b29bb8c4f, UTF-16LE, NV+BS+RT) set to `debian-6.12.efi` before boot → the foreign UKI boots. Set the variable in the vars file with virt-fw-vars if the installed version can, otherwise from a first boot of a helper UKI that writes it through efivarfs.
  S8 one-shot: S1 with LoaderEntryOneShot=`vintner-recovery-*` → recovery-a boots once, the variable is gone afterwards, and the next boot is os-2.
  S9 one-shot with recovery A bad: S8 with recovery-a+0-3 → recovery-b.
  S10 image fails to load: os-2+3 truncated to 4 KiB, os-1 → record what systemd-boot and OVMF do (the ADR predicts: os-2 becomes +2-1, systemd-boot exits to the firmware without trying os-1). This scenario records observed behaviour; it passes if the run completes and the behaviour is recorded.
  S11 key press: S1, send a key through the QEMU monitor (`sendkey spc`) during the first second → record whether the menu appears on serial with the entry titles. Observation only, like S10.
- Write ci/out/selection-policy/summary.tsv (scenario, boots, booted ids in order, final /EFI/Linux listing, PASS/FAIL/OBSERVED) and keep each scenario's serial logs.
- ci/selection-policy/README.md: purpose, how to run, required host packages, the trixie package versions used, and a results table from one run with the S10 and S11 observations written out.

Do not:
- touch any path outside ci/selection-policy/ (in particular not firmware/, docs/, ci/README.md, ci/lib/, ci/qemu-*, .github/, .gitignore, debian/, third_party/ or .jules/); if you think firmware/uefi/loader.conf or the ADR is wrong, say so in the PR description instead of changing them
- enable Secure Boot (a later task adds signed variants)
- use Docker or add language runtimes; bash, coreutils, curl, dpkg-deb, cpio, mtools, sfdisk, qemu, plus python3 only if ukify needs it
- commit generated images, debs or logs

Acceptance: `shellcheck ci/selection-policy/*.sh` is clean; `bash ci/selection-policy/build.sh && bash ci/selection-policy/run.sh` exits 0, with S1-S9 PASS and S10, S11 OBSERVED. If a scenario fails because systemd-boot behaves differently from ADR-0003, do not change the expectation to make it pass: report the scenario as FAIL, explain the observed behaviour in the PR description, and let run.sh exit non-zero. Paste summary.tsv into the PR description.

title: grubenv tear and power-cut experiments
prompt:
Measure how GRUB 2's grubenv behaves under abrupt resets and torn writes when it lives on a FAT boot storage partition, booting under SeaBIOS in QEMU.

Context: docs/architecture.md §4 (BIOS paragraph) puts the BIOS trial/fallback state in `grubenv` on a plain, unencrypted FAT32 boot storage partition; §12 risk 3 says retry atomicity is unverified (the 1 KiB environment block can tear across two 512-byte sectors) and must be tested with abrupt resets. This task produces evidence only; it does not design the vintner GRUB configuration.

Do:
- ci/grubenv/build.sh (bash; uses sudo for losetup/grub-install if needed): fetch grub-pc-bin and grub2-common from Debian trixie (deb.debian.org; record versions) and use those binaries and modules, not the host's. Build a raw disk image: GPT with a 2 MiB BIOS Boot Partition (type 21686148-6449-6e6f-744e-656564454649) and a 64 MiB boot storage partition (type bc13c2ff-59e6-4262-a352-b275fd6f7172, FAT32). Install GRUB for i386-pc with its prefix on the boot storage partition (/grub), serial console enabled (`serial --unit=0 --speed=115200; terminal_input serial; terminal_output serial`). Create /grub/grubenv with `grub-editenv`.
- Experiment E1, synthetic tears: produce a "before" grubenv (variable PAYLOAD=<450 x "a">, GEN=old) and an "after" grubenv (PAYLOAD=<450 x "b">, GEN=new), both exactly 1024 bytes. For each of the four combinations of sector 1 and sector 2 (old/old, old/new, new/old, new/new), write that block into the file's on-disk location, boot with a grub.cfg that runs `load_env` and prints `GEN=${GEN} PAYLOAD_HEAD=<first 8 chars if obtainable> LOADENV_RC=$?` (use whatever GRUB 2.12 script can express; the point is to see what load_env yields) and then `halt`. Also record `grub-editenv <file> list` output on the host for each combination.
- Experiment E2, random kills: a grub.cfg that runs `load_env`, flips GEN between old and new and PAYLOAD between the "a" and "b" fills, runs `save_env GEN PAYLOAD`, prints the value it saved, and then `reboot`s. Run QEMU (SeaBIOS, -nographic, serial to a file, `-drive file=...,format=raw,cache=writethrough`) and SIGKILL it at a random moment, for at least 300 iterations with uniformly random delays across the save_env window (calibrate the window from serial timestamps first; use TCG and KVM if /dev/kvm is usable, and note which). After every kill, extract grubenv with mtools and classify it: valid-old, valid-new, torn-but-parseable (state which variables survived), invalid. Count each class.
- Experiment E3, file placement: show whether `save_env` works when grubenv is (a) a normal 1024-byte file, (b) fragmented across non-adjacent clusters (use a small cluster size, 512 bytes, to force it), (c) replaced by a 0-byte file or missing. Record GRUB's error messages.
- ci/grubenv/README.md: method, trixie package versions, host QEMU version, and the results: E1 table, E2 counts per class, E3 observations, plus a short "implications" paragraph stating facts only (for example "a torn block was observed N times; in that case load_env did X").

Do not:
- touch any path outside ci/grubenv/ (in particular not firmware/, docs/, ci/README.md, ci/lib/, ci/qemu-*, .github/, .gitignore, debian/, third_party/ or .jules/)
- design or commit a production grub.cfg; the test configs live only under ci/grubenv/
- use Docker or add language runtimes; bash, coreutils, curl, dpkg-deb, mtools, sfdisk, qemu
- commit generated images or logs

Acceptance: `shellcheck ci/grubenv/*.sh` is clean; `bash ci/grubenv/build.sh && bash ci/grubenv/run.sh` exits 0 and writes ci/out/grubenv/results.tsv. Paste the E1 table, the E2 counts and the E3 observations into the PR description. If an experiment cannot be run as described, say exactly why in the PR description rather than substituting a different experiment silently.
